BUG_DIFF rewrites uid.py into an older API shape: it adds a module __getattr__ deprecation shim warning that "in pydicom v3.0 the UID for JPEGLossless will change", renames JPEGLossless to JPEGLosslessP14, and deletes the newer fragmentable-MPEG, JPEG XL, HTJ2K and SMPTE UIDs, then updates the two handlers to the old name (CODE_CONTEXT_01, CODE_CONTEXT_02). BUG_DIFF replaces StyleGuide.excluded's expand_paths-based check, which tested both the bare filename and the parent-joined path against the configured exclude/filename patterns, with a single call to self._file_checker_manager.is_path_excluded on the joined path (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 130-132). The documented behaviour - excluded if either form matches - is gone, and the new call depends on a manager method the packet does not show exists. BUG_DIFF removes the `-tm/--test-missing` argument, its incompatibility check with --test-folder="", and the block that disables test_package when the binary was not built from source (CODE_CONTEXT_01). A documented `conan create` option and its behaviour no longer exist; SPECIFICATION and TEST_FAILURE_01/02 (test_package only on build) cover the regression.

BUG_DIFF rewrites WSGIHeaderDict.__getitem__ to return the environ value as-is on Python 3 unless it is bytes, dropping the `val.encode('latin1').decode('utf8')` step (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Under the WSGI data contract environ headers are native strings decoded as latin-1, so UTF-8 header values must be re-decoded; the new code assumes the values are already correct text, producing mojibake like the 'Ã¶Ã¤Ã¼' in SPECIFICATION (TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF replaces the ordered-subtraction logic in GPXTrackPoint.time_difference with `total_seconds(self.time - track_point.time)` (CODE_CONTEXT_01), so the result is now signed and negative when the argument is later. The method's documented contract - an absolute difference in seconds, relied on by speed_between and add_missing_speeds - is regressed (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_03).

BUG_DIFF rewrites Optional.__init__: `self.key` is now the raw schema object instead of str(self._schema), the TypeError guard requiring a COMPARABLE schema for defaulted keys is removed, and an error=None kwarg is injected (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Schema.validate applies defaults by matching Optional.key against dict keys, so with a Literal or non-string key the default is never inserted; behaviour the library already promised is regressed (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_02).

BUG_DIFF inserts a check in analyze_lvalue that reports "can't assign to ()" for any empty TupleExpr before delegating to analyze_tuple_or_list_lvalue (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 4260-4263). Assignment to an empty tuple is legal in the Python versions mypy targets, and the checker already reports the correct '"int" object is not iterable' error for `() = 42`; the added diagnostic rests on an outdated assumption about language semantics and produces a spurious extra error (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF rewrites Worksheet.batch_update to split the request into a `params` dict (valueInputOption etc.) and a body containing only data, then calls self.client.values_batch_update(self.spreadsheet_id, params=params, body=body) (CODE_CONTEXT_01). The existing client method takes the whole request as `body`, and the Sheets values:batchUpdate API carries those options in the body, so the call raises TypeError (SPECIFICATION) and would send the wrong shape even if it did not. The change rests on an incorrect assumption about the client API and data contract (TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF swaps operands at several independent sites in PtyProcess.spawn (CODE_CONTEXT_01): both error messages now apply `%` with the data on the left and the format string on the right, so the FileNotFoundError and the bad-error-data Exception raise TypeError instead, and the closerange pairing becomes zip([2]+fds, [max_fd]+fds), which closes the wrong ranges and drops passed file descriptors. Each site regresses behaviour the class already promised (SPECIFICATION; TEST_FAILURE_01 invalid binary, 03 preexec error, 04 pass_fds). The scattered operand swaps are not themselves a defined pattern.

BUG_DIFF replaces HtmlFormatter._get_css_classes' loop, which walked a non-standard token type up to its STANDARD_TYPES ancestor and emitted every class along the way, with a single _get_ttype_class lookup (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Custom token types such as Name.Blubb now yield only their own class instead of "n n-Blubb", so stylesheets keyed on the hierarchical classes break; SPECIFICATION and TEST_FAILURE_01 (-F highlight option) cover the regression.

BUG_DIFF removes the `brackets = []`, `inside_quotes = False` and `path = path[4:]` initialisations from _path_to_elements while the loop still reads inside_quotes and appends to brackets (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 55-110), so the parser raises UnboundLocalError; it also replaces several `elem += char` accumulations with `pass` and drops the `prev_char = char` update. The deletions were not propagated to the surviving uses, so every path string fails to parse (TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_09 among 122).

BUG_DIFF rewrites X509Extension.__str__ so that a critical extension is rendered as "critical,<text>" and a failed X509V3_EXT_print returns an "<unprintable extension value ...>" placeholder instead of asserting (CODE_CONTEXT_01). The documented representation - the bare extension text, e.g. 'CA:FALSE' for a critical basicConstraints - is regressed (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01). The added prefix is extra behaviour that itself constitutes the defect.

The condition and both expressions are intact; only their pairing is inverted, so generated ids fail validation. No defined pattern describes a localised branch-body swap (TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF deletes the `if len(chunk_size) == 0: raise InvalidChunkSize` guard in ChunkedReader.parse_chunk_size (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 94-97). An empty chunk size line now reaches int(chunk_size, 16) and raises a bare ValueError instead of the parser's InvalidChunkSize, so the documented rejection of malformed chunked requests is regressed (SPECIFICATION; TEST_FAILURE_01/02 chunked_12 and chunked_13 invalid-request fixtures).

BUG_DIFF removes IoTDataPlaneResponse.setup_class, the override that passed use_raw_body=True to BaseResponse so publish payloads stay as bytes (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Without it the base class decodes the body as UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 payloads such as b'\xbf' raise UnicodeDecodeError; binary publishing the mock already supported is regressed (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF deletes the line that reads the `tools.files.download:verify` conf value into `verify` in conan.tools.files.download, while the neighbouring retry and retry_wait conf lookups remain (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 203-207). The documented configuration that lets users toggle SSL verification for downloads is silently ignored; SPECIFICATION and TEST_FAILURE_01 (download verify ssl conf) cover the regression.

proposed_other_pattern: Local logic mutation - statement reordering that reads locals before their definitions and moves the return ahead of the logic it depends on, with no misunderstanding or propagation aspect.
reasoning_summary: BUG_DIFF shuffles the statements of AccessTokenEndpoint.validate_access_token_request (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 119-215): valid_client and v are read before they are assigned, `return v, request` sits mid-method with the client/token validation and the final all(...) computation unreachably after it, and the transport and mandatory-parameter checks run after the signature check. The same statements are all still present; only their order is wrong, so the method raises UnboundLocalError. No defined pattern describes a wholesale statement-ordering defect (TEST_FAILURE_02, TEST_FAILURE_05).

BUG_DIFF reduces duration_isoformat to `return strftime(tduration, format)`, deleting the block that prefixes "-" for negative Duration or timedelta values (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Negative durations that previously round-tripped as "-P1DT2H3M4S" now lose their sign, so the parse/format symmetry the library promises is regressed (SPECIFICATION; TEST_FAILURE_01 and the negative test_format_parse cases such as TEST_FAILURE_02).

BUG_DIFF rewrites get_dependencies to dispatch on FileType.VIRTUAL_ENV, FileType.REQUIREMENTS and FileType.PYTHON and to call a read_requirements function; none of these exist in the repository, whose members are REQUIREMENTS_TXT, POETRY_LOCK, PIPENV_LOCK, PYPROJECT_TOML and VIRTUAL_ENVIRONMENT and whose reader is read_dependencies (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Accessing the missing enum members raises AttributeError, so no file type yields dependencies. The change rests on an incorrect model of the module's API (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF rewrites two internal modules to an earlier pydantic layout: the max_digits/decimal_places validators and NUMERIC_VALIDATOR_LOOKUP are removed from _validators.py in favour of a smaller _CONSTRAINT_TO_VALIDATOR_LOOKUP and get_constraint_validator (CODE_CONTEXT_02), and apply_known_metadata is reworked to call add_js_update_schema, which is not defined anywhere in the buggy module (CODE_CONTEXT_01). The surrounding package still expects the current names, so the suite fails at collection (SPECIFICATION; all 5438 tests, TEST_FAILURE_01). The edit is written against a different revision of these files than the one it was applied to.

BUG_DIFF deletes the "add a tail slice" step at the end of _slice_source_file_using_patches (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 330-339), so when the last patch ends before end-of-file the returned slices stop there and the remaining source is dropped from the fixed output. The method's promise that its slices partition the entire raw source, which _build_up_fixed_source_string depends on, is regressed (TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_02).

BUG_DIFF removes the whole `while chars:` trie-walking loop from Tokenizer._scan_keywords (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 1180-1200), so `word` is never set and multi-character keywords, spaced keywords and comment/string starters are no longer matched; every input degrades to single tokens and variables. Tokenization the library already guaranteed is regressed (TEST_FAILURE_04 space keywords, TEST_FAILURE_05 line/col, among 5).

BUG_DIFF rewrites Scope.ref_count to count every Scope found in `scope.sources`, i.e. every source visible to the scope, instead of the `selected_sources` that a scope actually references (CODE_CONTEXT_01). In this optimizer those two attributes differ by design, so CTEs referenced once are reported as multiply referenced and eliminate_ctes no longer inlines them. The rewrite rests on an incorrect assumption about the semantics of the Scope data model (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_02).

BUG_DIFF replaces PDFStructElement.to_dict's asdict-based serialisation with a hand-built dict containing only children and, if present, role_map/class_map (CODE_CONTEXT_01). The dataclass fields that define an element - type, revision, id, lang, alt_text, actual_text, title, page_number, attributes, mcids - are no longer emitted, so the documented dictionary representation consumed by the structure tests and the CLI converter is regressed (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_02, TEST_FAILURE_04 among 10).

BUG_DIFF removes the loop in Components._resolve_refs_in_parameter_or_header that resolved schema references inside each media type of a parameter's `content` (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 343-346), while the sibling request-body resolver still handles content. OpenAPI v3 parameters with content schemas now keep the raw schema name instead of a $ref, a resolution the library already promised (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF replaces `**(default_kwargs | engine_kwargs)` in OpenpyxlReader.load_workbook with explicit read_only/data_only/keep_links keywords followed by `**engine_kwargs` (CODE_CONTEXT_01). When a user passes any of those keys in engine_kwargs Python raises "got multiple values for keyword argument" instead of letting the user value override the default, so the documented ability to set data_only=False or read_only=False is lost. The change assumes call-site keyword merging semantics the language does not have (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_03).

BUG_DIFF rewrites _container_getitem and removes the `except ValueError` and `except TypeError` handlers that translated indexing errors into AstroidValueError/AstroidTypeError; only IndexError is still wrapped, and only for Const indices (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Applying a zero-step slice to elts now raises a bare ValueError out of inference instead of the Astroid exception callers catch, regressing the inference error contract (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01).

BUG_DIFF moves the generated docstring in pass_meta_key from the returned `decorator` onto the inner `new_func`, where update_wrapper immediately replaces it with the wrapped function's own __doc__, and changes the wording so the ":attr:`click.Context.meta`" reference and "to the decorated function" suffix are gone; it also swaps ctx.invoke(f, ...) for a direct call (CODE_CONTEXT_01). BUG_DIFF rewrites date_of_birth and deletes the TypeError/ValueError guards on minimum_age and maximum_age (negative values, non-integers, minimum greater than maximum), and also narrows the generated window by dropping the maximum_age + 1 boundary handling (CODE_CONTEXT_01). Invalid ages the method previously rejected are now silently accepted; SPECIFICATION and TEST_FAILURE_01 (value errors) cover the lost validation contract.

BUG_DIFF removes the `or not os.path.exists(frame.f_code.co_filename)` clause from the frame walk in find_dotenv (CODE_CONTEXT_01, lines 299-305). That clause existed so callers whose code lives inside a zip archive (no real file on disk) are skipped over when locating the caller's directory; without it find_dotenv resolves a path inside the archive and load_dotenv fails for zip-imported modules, a case the library already supported (SPECIFICATION, TEST_FAILURE_01, TEST_FAILURE_02).
